items.followUp: Why does atomic size generally decrease across a period?

rubric.why: Identifies the increase in nuclear charge across a period.
rubric.description: Nuclear charge increases from left to right across a period.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that nuclear or effective nuclear charge increases.

rubric.why: Links the increased nuclear charge to the attraction of an added electron and the trend in electron affinity.
rubric.description: The nucleus attracts an added electron more strongly, so electron affinity generally increases.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the stronger attraction causes electron affinity to increase.

modelAnswer: Across a period, nuclear charge and effective nuclear charge increase while the added electron enters the same main energy level.
The nucleus attracts the added electron more strongly, so electron affinity generally increases from left to right.

items.followUp: What are crystalline solids? Give an example.

accept: not arranged in a regular pattern
rubric.why: Identifies the characteristic arrangement of particles in an amorphous solid.
rubric.description: The constituent particles are not arranged in a regular pattern.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the particles as irregularly or randomly arranged.

rubric.why: Provides a suitable example of an amorphous solid.
rubric.description: Glass is a common example of an amorphous solid.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving a valid example such as glass, rubber, or plastic.

modelAnswer: Amorphous solids are solids whose constituent particles are not arranged in a regular pattern.
Glass is an example of an amorphous solid.

items.followUp: What types of substances dissolve best in polar solvents?

rubric.why: States the similarity principle behind the rule.
rubric.description: Substances with similar properties, especially similar polarity, tend to dissolve in one another.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that substances with similar properties or polarity dissolve in one another.

accept: polar substances dissolve in polar solvents
non-polar substances dissolve in non-polar solvents
rubric.why: Gives a valid application of the rule.
rubric.description: Polar substances dissolve in polar solvents, while non-polar substances dissolve in non-polar solvents.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving either valid polar/non-polar pairing.

modelAnswer: “Like dissolves like” means that substances with similar properties, especially similar polarity, dissolve in one another.
Thus, polar substances dissolve in polar solvents and non-polar substances dissolve in non-polar solvents.
